subject: Discovery Recap: Multi-tenancy controls (rate limits, quotas, routing)
messages:
From: Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.com>
To: Alex Jones <alex.jones@acme-corp.com>
Cc: Ben Carter <ben.carter@redwood.com>, Laura Bennett <laura.bennett@redwood.com>
Date: Sat, 10 Apr 2027 14:05:00 -0700
Subject: Discovery recap: multi-tenancy controls (rate limits, quotas, per-customer routing)

Hi Alex + Priya,

Great to meet today — thanks for taking the time. Below is a quick recap from our discovery and the items we agreed to follow up on. Please flag anything I missed.

Pain points you shared:
- Lack of per-customer rate limiting & quotas causing noisy tenants to impact overall latency.
- Current stack (self-hosted inference on k8s) struggles with bursty traffic and lacks cost isolation.
- No easy way to route high-value customers to higher SLAs without provisioning separate clusters.

Current stack / constraints:
- Inference: self-managed GPU fleet (NVIDIA A100) behind an internal API gateway.
- Auth: internal SSO (SAML) + per-org API keys; no tenant-level network isolation today.
- Compliance: SOC2 in progress; must enforce audit logs & key management for PII workloads.

Success criteria for a POC with Redwood:
- Ability to set per-customer rate limits and quotas (requests/min and token/day).
- Per-customer routing policy to send premium customers to dedicated capacity with <150ms median token latency.
- Clear cost attribution per tenant and tooling to enforce tiering policies (free vs paid).
- Audit logs and KMS integration for encrypted model access.

Next steps we agreed:
1) I will send a mutual action plan and a short doc on Redwood's multi-tenancy controls (attached).
2) You to share a sample of traffic profiles for 3 pilot customers (expected RPS, burst characteristics).
3) Tech sync week of Apr 19 to deep-dive routing & quota configuration with your infra lead.
4) Redwood to propose POC scope and high-level pricing for a 6-week evaluation.

Attachments: Mutual_Action_Plan_Acme.xlsx (MVP scope), redwood-multi-tenancy-controls.pdf (feature details).

If that aligns, I can get Ben (solution architect) looped in to work up the POC config.

Thanks again — talk soon.

Best,
Marissa
Account Executive | Redwood Inference
marissa.cole@redwood.com
+1 (415) 555-0184

Subject: Re: Discovery recap: multi-tenancy controls (rate limits, quotas, per-customer routing)

Thanks Marissa — this looks correct and very helpful. A few clarifications from our side: 

- For rate limits we need both soft (throttle) and hard (reject) thresholds per organization. Throttles should return a standard 429 with a Retry-After header.
- Quotas: want token-based daily/monthly quotas and alerting when usage hits 80% of quota.
- Routing: for premium customers we want automatic spillover to a dedicated capacity pool during sustained bursts; on short spikes (<5s) we prefer queued bursts vs cold-starting extra nodes.

On the compliance side, our security lead asked for sample audit log schema and confirmation that KMS can be customer-managed (we have an AWS KMS SEP in our account).

I'll pull together traffic samples for the three pilots and send by EOD on Monday Apr 12.

One Q: do you support per-tenant model pinning (i.e., pin premium customers to a tuned Llama variant)?

Alex
Director of Platform Engineering
Acme Corp

Subject: Re: Discovery recap: multi-tenancy controls (rate limits, quotas, per-customer routing)

Thanks Alex — great questions. Quick answers inline and a few notes on implementation options: 

- Soft vs hard limits: Yes — Redwood supports configurable rate-limit policies per-tenant with both throttling (429 + Retry-After) and hard rejection. Policies can be configured by route and per API key.

- Token-based quotas & alerts: We support token/day and token/month quotas with webhook alerting and threshold rules (80%, 90%). We can also tie quota usage to billing buckets for cost attribution.

- Routing + spillover: You can define routing policies that prefer dedicated capacity for premium tenants and configure spillover rules (queueing threshold, max queued requests, or fallback to hosted low-latency path). Short spikes can be handled with burst queues to avoid cold-starts.

- Per-tenant model pinning: Supported. You can pin a tenant to a specific model variant or quantized profile; we expose model pins as part of the routing policy so premium tenants can be directed to tuned models.

- KMS & audit logs: We support customer-managed KMS (AWS KMS) for key material and provide structured audit logs (timestamp, tenant_id, request_id, action, model_id). I'll attach a short schema sample in the doc I sent.

Attached are: redwood-multi-tenancy-controls.pdf (features & config examples) and a one-page mutual action plan that maps the POC milestones.

Proposed next steps:
- Tech sync: Apr 20 or 21 — Ben can lead the configuration session and demo the routing UI + policy YAML.
- You send traffic samples by Mon Apr 12 (we'll use that to size dedicated pool and propose burst configs).

If that works, I'll add the tech sync to the mutual action plan and send a calendar invite.

Best,
Marissa

Attachments: redwood-multi-tenancy-controls.pdf, Mutual_Action_Plan_Acme.xlsx

Alex
